Test Scenario and Description: Job Listing Accuracy and Metadata Display
Preconditions: Application server running and mock jobs loaded.
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to /index.html. 2. Verify page title and header logo. 3. Count visible job cards. 4. Verify title, salary, experience, location, and department for first job.
Expected Result: Page displays 4 job cards. 'Senior QA Automation Engineer' card accurately displays $130,000 - $160,000 / year, 5+ years experience, Remote / New York, NY, and Quality Engineering.
Actual Result: Rendered all 4 job cards with exact matching title, compensation, experience, and department metadata.

Test Scenario and Description: Dynamic Job Keyword Search and Filter
Preconditions: User is on job listings page with multiple positions loaded.
Test Steps: 1. Locate search input field. 2. Type 'QA'. 3. Verify filtered card count. 4. Type 'NonExistentRoleXYZ'. 5. Verify no jobs found message.
Expected Result: Search dynamically filters list to 1 card for 'QA'. Typing non-existent role displays 'No job positions match your criteria' and counter shows '0 open positions'.
Actual Result: Search input filtered positions dynamically without page reload. Empty state displayed when no match found.

Test Scenario and Description: Navigation to Correct Job Details Page via Apply Button
Preconditions: User is on job listings page /index.html.
Test Steps: 1. Locate 'Full Stack Software Engineer' card. 2. Click 'Apply Now' button. 3. Verify URL changes to job.html?id=fullstack-102. 4. Verify details title, salary, department, and requirements.
Expected Result: Browser navigates to /job.html?id=fullstack-102. Title shows 'Full Stack Software Engineer', salary '$140,000 - $175,000 / year', and 3 qualifications are listed. Hidden input #jobId is set.
Actual Result: Successfully navigated to matching job details page with exact title, compensation, and qualifications.

Test Scenario and Description: Return to Job Listings via Back Breadcrumb Link
Preconditions: User is on job details page /job.html?id=qa-eng-101.

Expected Result: Browser returns to /index.html and displays all available job listings.

Test Scenario and Description: Navigation with Non-Existent Job ID

Test Scenario and Description: Empty Required Form Fields Validation on Submission
Preconditions: User is on job application form for an open position.
Test Steps: 1. Navigate to /job.html?id=qa-eng-101. 2. Leave Full Name, Email, Phone, and Resume empty. 3. Click 'Submit Application'. 4. Check error messages and styling.
Expected Result: Inline error messages displayed under Full Name, Email, Phone, and Resume upload. Inputs highlighted with error styling. Form is not submitted.
Actual Result: Client-side validation caught all 4 empty required fields with clear messages and error borders. No network request sent.

Test Scenario and Description: Whitespace-Only Full Name Input Rejected

Expected Result: Full name input flagged with error 'Full name is required'. Submission aborted.

Test Scenario and Description: Full Name Minimum Length Boundary Violation

Expected Result: Error message displayed: 'Full name must be between 2 and 100 characters'. Form not submitted.
Actual Result: Boundary validation caught single-character entry and displayed length constraint message.

Test Scenario and Description: Invalid Email Format Missing Domain Rejected

Expected Result: Error message displayed: 'Please enter a valid email address (e.g. user@example.com)'. Form not submitted.
Actual Result: Regex email validation rejected malformed email address and displayed user-friendly guidance.

Test Scenario and Description: Incomplete Phone Number Under 10 Digits Rejected
Preconditions: User is on job application form.

Expected Result: Error message displayed: 'Please enter a valid phone number (at least 10 digits)'. Form not submitted.
Actual Result: Phone length constraint caught incomplete number and prevented submission.

Test Scenario and Description: Disallowed File Extension (.exe) Rejected for Resume Upload
Preconditions: User is on job application form.
Test Steps: 1. Fill valid name, email, and phone. 2. Select 'invalid_file.exe' for resume upload. 3. Click 'Submit Application'.
Expected Result: Error message displayed: 'Resume must be a .pdf, .docx, .doc, or .txt file'. Submission halted.
Actual Result: File extension check rejected .exe file and displayed allowed formats (.pdf, .docx, .doc, .txt).

Test Scenario and Description: Successful Application Submission Happy Path with Reference ID
Preconditions: User is on job application form for qa-eng-101.
Test Steps: 1. Fill all valid fields with real-world candidate data. 2. Attach sample_resume.pdf. 3. Click 'Submit Application'. 4. Verify success banner and reference ID. 5. Verify backend database record count and data.
Test Data: Name: Alice Walker, Email: alice.walker@example.com, Phone: +1 555-234-5678, Resume: sample_resume.pdf, Cover: 'Experienced QA engineer'
Expected Result: Success alert banner displayed with generated reference ID (APP-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX). Form fields cleared. Exactly 1 record saved in backend database with matching data.
Actual Result: Application submitted successfully; reference ID generated; verified 1 record persisted in backend with identical candidate info.

Test Scenario and Description: Duplicate Submission Prevention for Same Job and Candidate Email
Preconditions: Application already submitted once for qa-eng-101 with candidate email.
Test Steps: 1. Submit initial application for qa-eng-101 with email b.miller@example.com. 2. Immediately attempt second submission with same email and job. 3. Verify UI error banner. 4. Query backend DB to verify record count.
Test Data: Job: qa-eng-101, Name: Bob Miller, Email: b.miller@example.com, Phone: +1 555-888-9999, Resume: sample_resume.pdf
Expected Result: First submission succeeds. Second submission displays 'Duplicate Submission Detected' banner. Crucially, backend store contains strictly 1 application record.
Actual Result: Second submission rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict; duplicate banner rendered; verified only 1 application record created in database.

Test Scenario and Description: Browser Page Refresh After Submission Maintains Clean State
Preconditions: User has successfully submitted an application.
Test Steps: 1. Complete valid submission on /job.html?id=qa-eng-101. 2. Observe success alert. 3. Reload browser page (F5/reload). 4. Verify form fields and alert state. 5. Check database record count.
Expected Result: Page reloads with empty form inputs. Success banner is not persisted or stuck. No duplicate application record created on reload.
Actual Result: Page reloaded cleanly with fresh form; no phantom or repeat submissions triggered; DB record count remained 1.

Test Scenario and Description: Server Error (HTTP 500) Handling and Zero Unintended Records
Preconditions: User is on application form with 500 error simulation enabled.
Test Steps: 1. Fill valid application data. 2. Check 'Simulate Server Error (HTTP 500)' option. 3. Click 'Submit Application'. 4. Verify error banner and submit button state. 5. Check backend database records.
Test Data: Name: Devon Smith, Email: devon.smith@example.com, Simulate 500: True
Expected Result: UI displays 'Server Error (500)' banner with retry instruction. Submit button re-enabled for retry. Zero records created in application database.
Actual Result: HTTP 500 error handled gracefully; clear user feedback shown; verified database remained completely empty (0 records created).

Test Scenario and Description: Network Connection Failure During Submission
Preconditions: User is submitting application when client network drops.
Test Steps: 1. Fill valid application fields. 2. Simulate client network disconnection (Playwright route.abort). 3. Click 'Submit Application'. 4. Check UI response and database records.
Test Data: Name: Elena Rostova, Email: elena.rostova@example.com, Network: Aborted
Expected Result: UI catches network exception and renders 'Network Error' alert with connectivity advice. Submit button re-enabled. Zero records created in database.
Actual Result: Network error caught and displayed cleanly; button re-enabled; verified 0 application records committed in backend.

Test Scenario and Description: Slow Response Handling and In-Flight Submit Button State
Preconditions: User is submitting application under slow network conditions (3s delay).
Test Steps: 1. Fill valid application data. 2. Check 'Simulate Slow Network (3s delay)'. 3. Click 'Submit Application'. 4. Inspect submit button state during flight. 5. Wait for completion and verify success.
Test Data: Name: Fiona Gallagher, Email: fiona.g@example.com, Delay: 3 seconds
Expected Result: Submit button immediately disables with label 'Submitting application...' preventing duplicate clicks. After 3s response arrives, success banner appears and record saved.
Actual Result: Button disabled and loading state rendered throughout request flight; success banner displayed upon completion; 1 record saved.
